newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto makes good progress in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto makes good progress in Q1.

text.p: Italian banking group Banco Ambroveneto has made "satisfactory progress" in the first quarter of 1997, the group's chairman Giovanni Bazoli told the company's shareholders meeting on Tuesday.
The bank saw a strong rise in managed funds and demand for client services in the first quarter of 1997, which compensated for the predicted fall in net interest income.
"The financial accounts are in line with the budget and for the exercise in course we see an operating result in line with that of 1996," Bazoli said.

By March 31, the bank said client deposits had risen 5.4 percent compared to the first quarter of 1996, while client loans had increased some 12 percent. The group saw managed funds has risen some 88 percent to 9.935 trillion lire.

Bazoli underlined the difficulties that faced the Italian banking system in 1997 with the fall in interest rates reflected in the fall of the net interest income which Ambroveneto hopes will be offset by contributions from other services.
